question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{41}{2}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{41}{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1} \\ 7{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{41}{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ - \frac{41}{2}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{41}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5(3)+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ {x}_{2} &=- \frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{11}{2}$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{41}{2} \\ -(3)+3\left(- \frac{11}{2}\right) &=- \frac{41}{2} \\ - \frac{39}{2} &=- \frac{41}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

$$
